Dear Mr. Leonsis,

The Pentagon recently designated Alibaba Group Holding Limited (Alibaba) as a Chinese military company due to Alibaba’s support to China’s military-civil fusion and its ties to China’s state-owned assets commission and Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT).1 China’s military-civil fusion seeks to make the PLA the world’s leading military, particularly through the implementation of “intelligentized warfare”. Technology companies such as Alibaba play important roles in this computing-focused military advancement. This U.S. government designation is a recognition that Alibaba represents a danger to American security and the stability of the western Pacific.

In one example of how Alibaba supports China’s military ambitions, its cloud and AI services enable China’s BeiDou satellite system to provide position, navigation, and timing to the People’s Liberation Army (PLA).2 Alibaba Cloud partners with a key contractor of BeiDou, and Alibaba has obscured its ownership of that same key contractor.3 In turn, the PLA is using
